newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Hanjin consortium wins 194.6 bln won deal.
newsitem.headline: Hanjin consortium wins 194.6 bln won deal.

text.p: A consortium of four firms, led by Hanjin Engineering and Construction Co, has won a 194.6 billion won contract to construct part of an airport passenger terminal, the Korea Airport Construction Authority said on Friday.
The consortium also included South Korea's Samsung Corp and Daewoo Corp, and Fluor Daniel Eastern of the United States, the authority said in a statement.
The statement said the consortium was among three international groups which had applied for the contract.

The firms will build the floor and frame structure of a passenger terminal at the Inchon International Airport, now under construction on an island off the western port city of Inchon, the statement said.
Construction on the airport began in 1992 and is scheduled to be completed by the end of 1999, with full-scale operations due to start in late 2000, an authority official said.
